question: Prvá železnica na území dnešného Slovenska viedla z Bratislavy do Trnavy. Čo však ťahalo jej vozne namiesto parnej lokomotívy?
source_excerpt: Pred 170 rokmi prišiel do Trnavy prvý vlak, ťahali ho kone

extra.why_interesting: Players picture 'first railway' as a smoking steam engine. The twist is that Slovakia's first railway ran on rails but was pulled by horses. A player can reason toward it: what pulled loads before steam?
extra.verification_notes: The first Slovak railway Bratislava–Trnava (opened 1846) was a horse-drawn line until steam replaced horses in 1872–73, per https://sita.sk/pred-170-rokmi-prisiel-do-trnavy-prvy-vlak-tahali-ho-kone/.

explanation: Bola to konská železnica: vozne na koľajniciach ťahali kone, lebo po hladkých koľajniciach utiahol jeden kôň oveľa viac než po hrboľatej ceste. Parné rušne prišli na Slovensko až neskôr.

question: Prečo sa v starších vlakoch ozývalo pravidelné „ťuk-ťuk, ťuk-ťuk“? Cez čo kolesá stále prechádzali?
source_excerpt: The sound is caused by train wheels passing over rail joints, which are used to hold sections of rail together.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows the 'ťuk-ťuk' sound of an old train but rarely asks what makes it. It can be worked out from everyday knowledge: metal expands in heat, so rails need gaps. Players also learn why modern trains no longer make that sound.
extra.verification_notes: The clickety-clack sound is caused by wheels crossing gaps/joints between rail sections, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_noise; welded rail has largely removed it.

explanation: Kovové koľajnice sa v lete od tepla rozťahujú, preto medzi nimi nechávali malé medzery a kolesá na každej ťukli. Dnes sa koľajnice zvárajú do dlhých súvislých pásov, a preto je jazda oveľa tichšia.
